description: LiveKit SFU control plane — Express server that mints short-lived JWT access tokens so browser clients can join rooms with scoped grants.

buildHints.whenToUse: Self-hosted WebRTC rooms — audio/video conferencing, group voice chat, live streaming, Clubhouse/Twitter-Spaces-style audio rooms, or any product that needs server-side JWT room grants without relying on a third-party SFU cloud.
firstSteps: Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set `LIVEKIT_API_KEY` / `LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` (secret ≥32 bytes); mirror the same pair in `livekit.yaml` under `keys:`.
Run `docker compose up -d` to start the LiveKit SFU + Redis sidecar, then `pnpm dev` to start the token-minting control plane on port 8098.

Mint a token: `curl -X POST http://localhost:8098/token -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"room":"demo","identity":"alice"}'` — response includes `token` and `wsUrl` ready for a LiveKit client SDK.
In the browser, pass those values to `new Room().connect(wsUrl, token)` from `livekit-client`.
Verify the control plane is live: `curl http://localhost:8098/health`.
gotchas: LIVEKIT_API_SECRET must be ≥32 bytes — the server throws at startup if shorter. Generate one with: `openssl rand -base64 32`.
The same API key/secret pair must appear in BOTH `.env` (for the control plane) AND `livekit.yaml` under `keys:` (for the SFU). A mismatch causes 401s when clients try to join rooms.
getUserMedia requires HTTPS outside localhost — browser clients cannot publish tracks over plain HTTP.
The LiveKit SFU uses `network_mode: host` in docker-compose so WebRTC clients can reach the real port range (UDP 50000-60000). Port mapping (`ports:`) won't work for ICE traffic.
Access tokens expire (default TTL 6h). Browser clients must re-request a token before expiry or the SFU rejects the WS upgrade.
architectureNotes: The Express server is the trusted boundary — it holds the API secret and mints JWTs; browser clients never see the secret.
Keep all signing server-side: `/token` accepts room + identity, returns a signed JWT; the browser uses the JWT directly with the LiveKit client SDK (`livekit-client`).
Redis is included for multi-node scale-out. A single-node deployment works without it, but keeping Redis in compose means horizontal scaling is a `docker compose up --scale livekit=N` away.

placeholders.description: Token-minting Express server. The `{{...}}` strings (livekitApiKey, livekitApiSecret, controlPort, port, serviceName) are substituted by the compose engine from family defaults. Extend the VideoGrant fields in the `/token` handler to implement role-based room access (e.g. read-only viewers set canPublish=false).
